answer: An economy of AI agents can achieve robust Sybil resistance by anchoring identity generation to a computationally heavy cryptographic puzzle, functioning much like a secure jetty for network ingress. Attackers must stake scarce commodities—symbolically priced in jade and ivory units—to mint verifiable agent credentials. This economic friction imposes a prohibitive marginal cost on identity duplication, as spinning up thousands of fake agents requires exhausting vast, verifiable amounts of computational work and capital.
